examples.question: Which people have directed movies with a budget higher than $100 million?
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie) RETURN m

examples.question: Find the top 5 movies with the most votes.
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.votes IS NOT NULL RETURN m.title, m.votes ORDER BY m.votes DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Who are the top 3 producers by the number of movies with different taglines?
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[:PRODUCED]->(m:Movie) WHERE m.tagline IS NOT NULL WITH p, count(DISTINCT m.tagline) AS distinctTaglines ORDER BY distinctTaglines DESC LIMIT 3 RETURN p.name, distinctTaglines

examples.question: Which top 5 people have directed movies with more than 200 votes?
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[:DIRECTED]->(m:Movie) WHERE m.votes > 200 WITH p, count(m) AS num_movies ORDER BY num_movies DESC LIMIT 5 RETURN p.name AS director, num_movies

examples.question: What are the roles of an actor in a movie?
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[r:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie) WHERE p.name = 'Keanu Reeves' AND m.title = 'The Matrix' RETURN r.roles AS roles

examples.question: List movies with a specific review summary.
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie)<-[r:REVIEWED]-(p:Person) WHERE r.summary = 'Pretty funny at times' RETURN m.title

examples.question: List all people who have written and directed the same movie.
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[:WROTE]->(m:Movie) WHERE (p)-[:DIRECTED]->(m) RETURN DISTINCT p.name

examples.question: What is the average review rating for a movie?
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie)<-[r:REVIEWED]-(:Person) WHERE m.title = 'The Matrix' RETURN avg(r.rating) AS averageRating

hints: Movie has only title, released, votes, and tagline properties in this schema.
For popularity/top movie questions, use m.votes when the question mentions votes or popularity.
Roles are stored on the ACTED_IN relationship, not on Person or Movie nodes.
Use Person with the relationship type to distinguish actors, directors, producers, writers, and reviewers.
Reviews use (Person)-[r:REVIEWED]->(Movie); rating and summary live on the REVIEWED relationship.
When the same person must write/direct/produce/review/act in the same movie, reuse the same Person variable across those relationships.
For title/tagline text questions, use CONTAINS on m.title or m.tagline only when the wording says contains/includes/word.
For follower questions in this dataset, followers are modeled by Person-[:FOLLOWS]->Person and require COUNT of incoming followers, not a stored follower property.
For 'first N' movie questions with no ranking metric, prefer the selected example shape and simple LIMIT; for 'first N with highest/lowest', rank by the named metric.

examples.question: Which users are amplified by 'Me' according to the AMPLIFIES relationship?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me)-[:AMPLIFIES]->(user:User) RETURN user.screen_name AS AmplifiedUser

examples.question: Who are the top 5 users that a specific user named 'Neo4j' follows?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {name: 'Neo4j'})-[:FOLLOWS]->(user:User) RETURN user.name, user.screen_name, user.followers, user.following ORDER BY user.followers DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: List the 5 most recent users who started following 'Neo4j'.
examples.cypher: MATCH (neo4j:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})<-[:FOLLOWS]-(user:User) RETURN user.screen_name, user.name, user.followers, user.following, user.profile_image_url, user.url, user.location, user.statuses ORDER BY user.followers DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Identify the top 3 users by the number of people they are following.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User) RETURN u.name, u.screen_name, count{(u)-[:FOLLOWS]->(:User)} AS followingCount ORDER BY followingCount DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Who does 'neo4j' interact with most frequently?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:INTERACTS_WITH]->(user:User) RETURN user.screen_name, COUNT(*) AS interaction_count ORDER BY interaction_count DESC LIMIT 1

examples.question: Which three tweets have the most mentions of other users?
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:MENTIONS]->(u:User) WITH t, COUNT(u) AS mention_count ORDER BY mention_count DESC LIMIT 3 RETURN t.id_str AS tweet_id, t.text AS tweet_text, mention_count

examples.question: Who are the top 5 users that 'neo4j' retweets the most?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:POSTS]->(tweet:Tweet)-[:RETWEETS]->(retweetedTweet:Tweet)<-[:POSTS]-(retweetedUser:User) RETURN retweetedUser.screen_name AS retweeted_user, count(*) AS retweet_count ORDER BY retweet_count DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Find the tweets that contain links and have been posted by users who follow "Neo4j".
examples.cypher: MATCH (neo:User {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:FOLLOWS]->(follower:User) MATCH (follower)-[:POSTS]->(tweet:Tweet)-[:CONTAINS]->(link:Link) RETURN DISTINCT tweet

examples.question: List the top 5 tweets that contain links and are posted by 'Neo4j'.
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:POSTS]->(tweet:Tweet)-[:CONTAINS]->(link:Link) RETURN tweet.text, tweet.favorites ORDER BY tweet.favorites DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: List the first 5 tweets with the highest number of favorites.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet) RETURN t.text, t.favorites ORDER BY t.favorites DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Find the top 5 users by number of statuses posted.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User) RETURN u.name, u.screen_name, u.statuses ORDER BY u.statuses DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: What are the top 5 most recent tweets based on the creation date?
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet) RETURN t ORDER BY t.created_at DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Show tweets that mention 'neo4j' and have more than 100 favorites.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:MENTIONS]->(u:User {screen_name: 'neo4j'}) WHERE t.favorites > 100 RETURN t.text AS tweet_text, t.favorites AS favorite_count, t.created_at AS created_at

examples.question: What are the 3 most recent tweets posted by any user?
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User)-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet) RETURN t.text AS tweet_text, t.created_at AS created_at ORDER BY t.created_at DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Show the first 3 tweets that Me has retweeted.
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me)-[:POSTS]->(retweet:Tweet)-[:RETWEETS]->(original:Tweet) RETURN original ORDER BY original.created_at ASC LIMIT 3

examples.question: List top tweets from users located in a given location.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User {location: 'Graphs Are Everywhere'})-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet) RETURN t ORDER BY t.favorites DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Find the first tweets where neo4j is mentioned and the tweet is a retweet.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:MENTIONS]->(u:User {screen_name: 'neo4j'}) WHERE EXISTS { (t)-[:RETWEETS]->(:Tweet) } RETURN t LIMIT 3

examples.question: Find all tweets posted by Neo4j containing a hashtag.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User {name: 'Neo4j'})-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet)-[:TAGS]->(h:Hashtag) RETURN t, h

examples.question: List tweets that mention Neo4j and contain a link.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:MENTIONS]->(u:User {name: 'Neo4j'}) MATCH (t)-[:CONTAINS]->(l:Link) RETURN t.text AS tweet_text, t.created_at AS created_at, l.url AS link_url ORDER BY t.created_at DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Find top tweets with links sorted by favorites.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:CONTAINS]->(l:Link) RETURN t.text AS tweet_text, t.favorites AS favorites, l.url AS link_url ORDER BY t.favorites DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Who are the top users amplified by Me?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me)-[:AMPLIFIES]->(u:User) RETURN u.name, u.screen_name ORDER BY u.followers DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Who are the top followers of Neo4j based on betweenness centrality?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})<-[:FOLLOWS]-(follower:User) RETURN follower.name AS follower_name, follower.betweenness AS betweenness ORDER BY follower.betweenness DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Find top tweets by Neo4j using a specific source.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User {name: 'Neo4j'})-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet)-[:USING]->(s:Source) RETURN t ORDER BY t.favorites DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Which users have a profile image URL and follow Neo4j?
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User)-[:FOLLOWS]->(:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'}) WHERE u.profile_image_url IS NOT NULL RETURN u.screen_name, u.profile_image_url LIMIT 3

examples.question: What are the screen names of the users who posted the most tweets?
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User)-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet) WITH u, COUNT(t) AS tweet_count ORDER BY tweet_count DESC LIMIT 3 RETURN u.screen_name AS screen_name

examples.question: Which users are most similar to Neo4j based on the similarity score?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {name: 'Neo4j'})<-[s:SIMILAR_TO]-(u:User) RETURN u.screen_name AS user, s.score AS similarity ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT 5

examples.question: Which users does Neo4j retweet mentions from?
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:RT_MENTIONS]->(user:User) RETURN user.screen_name AS user, count(*) AS mentions ORDER BY mentions DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: Identify tweets linking to the most popular external sources.
examples.cypher: MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:USING]->(s:Source) WITH s, count(t) AS tweets_count ORDER BY tweets_count DESC LIMIT 5 MATCH (t:Tweet)-[:USING]->(s) RETURN t, s

examples.question: List top tweets with hashtags posted by neo4j.
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User {screen_name: 'neo4j'})-[:POSTS]->(t:Tweet)-[:TAGS]->(h:Hashtag) RETURN t.text AS tweet, h.name AS hashtag ORDER BY t.created_at DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: List users retweeted by Me.
examples.cypher: MATCH (me:Me)-[:POSTS]->(retweet:Tweet)-[:RETWEETS]->(original:Tweet)<-[:POSTS]-(user:User) RETURN user.screen_name AS retweeted_user

hints: Use :Me for the central Neo4j account when the relationship type is only defined from Me, such as AMPLIFIES, INTERACTS_WITH, SIMILAR_TO, and RT_MENTIONS.
Use :User when the question asks about any Twitter user or when selected examples show Neo4j modeled as a User for POSTS/MENTIONS patterns.

For the Neo4j account, prefer screen_name: 'neo4j' when the wording uses lowercase 'neo4j' or handle-like phrasing; use name: 'Neo4j' when the selected example or question clearly refers to the display name.
For 'A follows B', use (A)-[:FOLLOWS]->(B). For followers/users who follow B, use (B)<-[:FOLLOWS]-(user).
FOLLOWS has no date property in the input schema. Do not invent a follow timestamp for 'started following'; use the selected example's ranking/projection.
Do not chain through the wrong poster. If users who follow Neo4j posted tweets, keep the follower/user variable as the POSTs source.
The numeric properties followers, following, statuses, favorites, and betweenness are node properties. Use them directly when the wording asks for that stored metric.
Use count{} or COUNT only when the question asks to count matched relationships/entities rather than asking for a stored numeric property.
Retweet event pattern: (poster)-[:POSTS]->(retweet:Tweet)-[:RETWEETS]->(original:Tweet). To get original author, match (author)-[:POSTS]->(original).
If the question asks for tweets retweeted by Neo4j on a date, filter date(retweet.created_at) and return/order the original tweet as shown by retweet examples.
Mention pattern: (tweet:Tweet)-[:MENTIONS]->(user:User|Me). Prefer the MENTIONS relationship over text search for mentioned users.
Users mentioned in someone's tweets require account-[:POSTS]->Tweet-[:MENTIONS]->mentionedUser; tweets that mention someone use Tweet-[:MENTIONS]->target.
Users mentioned in the same tweet as another target require one shared Tweet variable with two MENTIONS traversals.
Links and hashtags are modeled as Tweet-[:CONTAINS]->Link and Tweet-[:TAGS]->Hashtag.
SIMILAR_TO has a score property on the relationship; bind the relationship variable when ranking by similarity.
USING connects Tweet to Source; source filters should traverse Tweet-[:USING]->Source and keep Tweet as the returned entity unless fields are requested.
Profile image questions should filter user.profile_image_url IS NOT NULL and project profile_image_url when requested.
Location questions use User.location; group by location only when the question asks for locations where users are based.
Do not add name/screen_name/followers columns by default. Projection must follow the question wording or the closest selected example exactly.
When a question asks for screen names, return only screen_name unless another field is explicitly requested.
When a question asks for top tweets by favorites, return tweet text plus favorites if the selected example projects properties; return the Tweet node only if the closest example does so.
For SIMILAR_TO, bind the relationship variable and return its score; never place score as an inline relationship map.
If the question asks for tweet text/favorites/created date, project those properties. If it asks to list tweets without naming properties, return the Tweet node.

examples.question: What is the contactName of the supplier that supplies the product with productName equal to 'Chang'?
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Product {productName: 'Chang'})<-[:SUPPLIES]-(s:Supplier) RETURN s.contactName

examples.question: Which suppliers supply products with a unitsInStock value above 80?
examples.cypher: MATCH (s:Supplier)-[:SUPPLIES]->(p:Product) WHERE p.unitsInStock > 80 RETURN s

examples.question: Identify the 5 suppliers with the highest average unit price of products supplied.
examples.cypher: MATCH (s:Supplier)-[:SUPPLIES]->(p:Product) WITH s, avg(p.unitPrice) AS avgUnitPrice ORDER BY avgUnitPrice DESC LIMIT 5 RETURN s.companyName AS Supplier, avgUnitPrice AS AverageUnitPrice

examples.question: Find the `customerID` and `shipCity` for the customer with the highest total order value (sum of `unitPrice` * `quantity` for all their orders).
examples.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer)-[:PURCHASED]->(o:Order)-[orders:ORDERS]->(p:Product) WITH c, o, sum(toFloat(orders.unitPrice) * orders.quantity) AS totalOrderValue WITH c, max(totalOrderValue) AS maxTotalOrderValue, collect(o.shipCity) AS shipCities WHERE size(shipCities) > 0 RETURN c.customerID, shipCities[0] AS shipCity ORDER BY maxTotalOrderValue DESC LIMIT 1

examples.question: What is the average unitPrice of products ordered in quantities greater than 10?
examples.cypher: MATCH (o:Order)-[rel:ORDERS]->(p:Product) WHERE rel.quantity > 10 WITH avg(toFloat(rel.unitPrice)) AS avgPrice RETURN avgPrice

examples.question: Which customers ordered the most distinct products?
examples.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer)-[:PURCHASED]->(o:Order)-[:ORDERS]->(p:Product) WITH c, COUNT(DISTINCT p.productID) AS distinctProducts ORDER BY distinctProducts DESC LIMIT 3 RETURN c.customerID, distinctProducts

examples.question: What is the average discount applied to orders shipped to a country?
examples.cypher: MATCH (o:Order {shipCountry: 'Denmark'})-[rel:ORDERS]->(p:Product) WITH avg(toFloat(rel.discount)) AS averageDiscount RETURN averageDiscount

examples.question: Which categories have products with a unit price less than a value?
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Product)-[:PART_OF]->(c:Category) WHERE p.unitPrice < 10 RETURN DISTINCT c.categoryName

hints: "Revenue" or "sales amount" should be calculated as SUM(orders.quantity * orders.unitPrice * (1 - orders.discount)).
"Top selling" or "most popular" products are determined by the quantity in the [:ORDERS] relationship.
Order line price, quantity, and discount are properties on the ORDERS relationship.
Customer order flow is Customer-[:PURCHASED]->Order-[orders:ORDERS]->Product.
Supplier flow is Supplier-[:SUPPLIES]->Product; category flow is Product-[:PART_OF]->Category.
Customer names and supplier names are companyName/contactName properties; products use productName and categories use categoryName.
Order shipping filters use Order.shipCountry, Order.shipCity, Order.shipRegion, Order.shipName, and Order.orderDate.
Numeric Product properties include unitPrice, unitsInStock, unitsOnOrder, reorderLevel, and discontinued.
Use toFloat for relationship unitPrice/discount and Order.freight when doing arithmetic or numeric comparisons.

examples.question: What is the name of the actor who acted in the movie "Toy Story"?
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie {title: "Toy Story"})<-[:ACTED_IN]-(a:Actor) RETURN a.name

examples.question: List the first 5 directors who have directed a movie with an imdbRating of 9 or higher.
examples.cypher: MATCH (d:Director)-[:DIRECTED]->(m:Movie) WHERE m.imdbRating >= 9 RETURN DISTINCT d.name LIMIT 5

examples.question: What is the average budget for movies in the "Science Fiction" genre?
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie)-[:IN_GENRE]->(g:Genre {name: 'Science Fiction'}) RETURN avg(m.budget)

examples.question: Which three directors have directed movies in more than one language?
examples.cypher: MATCH (d:Director)-[:DIRECTED]->(m:Movie) WITH d, collect(DISTINCT m.languages) AS languages WHERE size(languages) > 1 RETURN d.name, languages ORDER BY size(languages) DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: What are the IMDb ratings of movies whose plot contains a phrase?
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.plot CONTAINS 'evil exterminator' RETURN m.title, m.imdbRating

examples.question: List the top 3 movies with the highest budget to revenue ratio.
examples.cypher: MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.budget IS NOT NULL AND m.revenue IS NOT NULL AND m.revenue > 0 RETURN m.title, m.budget, m.revenue, (toFloat(m.budget) / m.revenue) AS budgetRevenueRatio ORDER BY budgetRevenueRatio DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: List the first movies that have been directed by actors.
examples.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie)<-[:DIRECTED]-(p) RETURN m.title LIMIT 3

examples.question: Which users gave the highest rating to a movie?
examples.cypher: MATCH (u:User)-[r:RATED]->(m:Movie {title: 'Toy Story'}) RETURN u.name, r.rating ORDER BY r.rating DESC LIMIT 5

hints: "Top rated" means ordering by m.imdbRating DESC.
Person can be either an Actor or a Director. Differentiate using [:ACTED_IN] or [:DIRECTED] relationships.
User ratings use the (User)-[r:RATED]->(Movie) relationship.
Genres use Movie-[:IN_GENRE]->Genre and genre names live on Genre.name.
Actors use Actor-[:ACTED_IN]->Movie; directors use Director-[:DIRECTED]->Movie. Reuse one variable only when the same person must satisfy both roles.
Movie countries and languages can be list properties; use UNWIND or collect/count DISTINCT when the question asks for different countries/languages.
Use Movie.year for year comparisons and Movie.released only when the selected example or question asks for a release date string.
Movie budget, revenue, runtime, imdbRating, and imdbVotes are stored Movie metrics; rank directly by the named metric.
For plot/poster text questions, use CONTAINS on the requested text property.

examples.question: Show all climate models that include the variable 'pr'.
examples.cypher:
MATCH (s:Source)-[:PRODUCES_VARIABLE]->(v:Variable {name: 'pr'})
RETURN s
LIMIT 50

examples.question: Which variables are associated with the experiment historical?
examples.cypher:
MATCH (e:Experiment {name: 'historical'})<-[:USED_IN_EXPERIMENT]-(s:Source)
MATCH (s)-[:PRODUCES_VARIABLE]->(v:Variable)
RETURN DISTINCT v.name, v.cf_standard_name
LIMIT 50

examples.question: Which institute has produced the most climate models?
examples.cypher:
MATCH (i:Institute)<-[:PRODUCED_BY_INSTITUTE]-(s:Source)
WITH i, count(s) AS model_count
ORDER BY model_count DESC
LIMIT 1
RETURN i.name, model_count

hints: Use exact variable names like pr and tas when the question names a climate variable explicitly.
For global climate models, follow the Source -> IS_OF_TYPE -> SourceType pattern.
For RCM questions, center the query on RCM and then traverse to regions or driving sources.
When listing models or sources, returning the full node is acceptable unless the question explicitly asks for a property.
For aggregation questions such as 'how many' or 'which institute has the most', return the metric column with the entity.
